name: kidney-model-simulation
title: Kidney model simulation — run every atlas-mapped kidney model in its compatible simulator
question:
Can we take the models the atlas maps to an organ — kidney — pull every one,
load each into its COMPATIBLE simulator (SBML BioModels under COPASI, CellML
Physiome models under OpenCOR), run each to a timeseries, and present all of
them together in one interactive dashboard that shows both the models that run
(with real trajectories) and the ones that don't (with the reason)?

study_card.goal: Consume the atlas's organ->models output for the kidney, route each model to its compatible simulator by format, run it, normalize the heterogeneous results, and render one interactive dashboard — no silent drops.
study_card.mechanism: OrganSimulationStep -> select_organ_models('kidney') pulls the 24 kidney-tagged runnable models from the BioModels/Physiome->HRA map (5 SBML BioModels, 19 CellML Physiome; PhysioNet entries are dataset references and excluded). SBML models run through viva_biomodels.run_comparison under COPASI (duration/points read from each model's own SED-ML); CellML models are resolved to their PMR .cellml URL (resolve_cellml_url) and run through viva_opencor.OpenCORUTCStep. Each run is isolated so one failure never sinks the batch; both result shapes are normalized to {time, series} and rendered as a grid of per-model cards (name, simulator, run-status badge) that expand into interactive Plotly timeseries. Failure cards show why a model didn't run.
study_card.expected_result: All 24 runnable kidney models attempted; a dashboard where every model is either a live timeseries or a labeled failure. Spike yield: ~9/19 Physiome models run via OpenCOR with the single-file CellML resolver (the rest fail on multi-file/import CellML or a dead exposure page), plus the BioModels that carry SED-ML.
study_card.main_expert_question: Is single-file-CellML + SED-ML-gated SBML the honest runnable subset of an organ's atlas models, or does fetching each Physiome exposure's full workspace fileset (for import-heavy CellML) materially raise the yield?

biological_summary:
The atlas tells you WHICH mechanistic models describe the kidney; this study
RUNS them. Kidney draws 24 runnable models from two repositories with two
formats: 5 SBML BioModels (e.g. the Tiago iron-metabolism series) and 19
CellML Physiome models (the classic Eskandari/Mackenzie Na+/glucose
cotransporter and Na+/K+-ATPase transporter models). Each is loaded into the
simulator its format demands — SBML under COPASI, CellML under OpenCOR — run to
a timeseries, and shown in one place. The result is deliberately honest: some
models run and produce trajectories; others fail (a BioModel with no SED-ML to
say how long to run, a CellML model whose imports the single-file fetch can't
satisfy, an exposure page that 500s), and the dashboard names each failure
rather than hiding it. This turns the atlas from a static map into a runnable
view of an organ's models.
readouts: kidney models attempted: 24 (5 SBML->COPASI, 19 CellML->OpenCOR; PhysioNet excluded)
per model: ran|failed, simulator, and (if ran) a normalized {time, series} timeseries
dashboard: one interactive page, a grid of per-model cards expanding to Plotly species/state plots; failure cards show the reason

report.title: Kidney model simulation — 24 atlas models routed to COPASI/OpenCOR, run, and shown in one dashboard
report.objective:
Run every runnable model the atlas maps to the kidney in its compatible
simulator and present all timeseries (and all failures) in one interactive
dashboard.
report.conclusion:
OrganSimulationStep pulls the kidney's 24 runnable models, routes each by
format (SBML->COPASI via viva_biomodels, CellML->OpenCOR via viva_opencor),
runs them in isolation, normalizes the two result shapes, and writes an
interactive dashboard: a grid of per-model cards, each a live Plotly
timeseries or a labeled failure. The libOpenCOR path is spike-validated
(~9/19 Physiome kidney models run cleanly with the single-file CellML
resolver); the BioModels that carry SED-ML run under COPASI. The machinery is
organ-parameterized — the same Step runs any organ the atlas covers.
report.caveat:
This is a LIVE run study: native COPASI + libOpenCOR engines and live PMR /
BioModels fetches, so it is not offline-reproducible and re-runs can differ
with upstream changes. The runnable subset is bounded by data, not method:
BioModels without SED-ML fail to load, and import-heavy CellML fails the
single-file resolver — fetching each Physiome exposure's full workspace
fileset is the named follow-up to lift the CellML yield.

embed_visualizations.description: Grid of per-model cards — SBML under COPASI, CellML under OpenCOR — each expanding to an interactive Plotly timeseries; failure cards show why a model didn't run.

findings.statement:
An organ's atlas-mapped models can be run end-to-end in their compatible
simulators from a single Step: the kidney's 24 runnable models (5 SBML, 19
CellML) route to COPASI and OpenCOR respectively, run in isolation, and
render as one interactive dashboard where each model is a live timeseries
or a labeled failure.

evidence.summary: OrganSimulationStep(organ=kidney): 24 models selected (PhysioNet excluded), SBML via viva_biomodels.run_comparison (COPASI, SED-ML durations), CellML via resolve_cellml_url + viva_opencor.OpenCORUTCStep. Spike: 9/19 Physiome run cleanly; results normalized to {time, series} and written to studies/kidney-model-simulation/viz/index.html.

limitations: Live run study (native COPASI + libOpenCOR, PMR/BioModels network): not offline-reproducible; the committed dashboard is a snapshot of one run.
CellML yield is bounded by the single-file resolver — import-heavy Physiome models fail to load until their full workspace fileset is fetched (named follow-up).
SBML models without SED-ML fail to load (the documented BioModels load-failure mode) and appear as failure cards.
